policies.name: Two-child norm with penalties (coercive)
policies.description: Penalise families with more than two children (loss of benefits, ineligibility for local office or government jobs).
benefits: Small additional reduction in fertility (evidence weak)
unintendedConsequences: Punishes children and poor families for parents' choices
Increases sex-selective abortion and abandonment of girls
Excludes women and marginalised groups from political office
policies.shortTerm: Immediate social backlash; exclusion of poorer households.
policies.longTerm: Distorted sex ratios, loss of trust in government, little extra fertility decline beyond voluntary trends.
policies.stateDifferences: Some Indian states have applied such rules to local-body elections; studies found weak fertility effects and harm to women.
policies.uncertainty: Very uncertain fertility effect; harms are well documented.
policies.humanRightsConcern: This is a coercive policy. It conflicts with reproductive rights recognised in international human-rights law (e.g. ICPD Programme of Action) and penalises children. The simulator models its social harms, not just its intended effect.
